vulnerabilities.description: Command injection vulnerability in glob 10.2.0-10.4.5 (GHSA-5j98-mcp5-4vw2): -c/--cmd executes matches with shell:true. Indirectly used via eslint-config-next. Update glob to >=11.0.0
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Update glob to version 11.0.0 or higher via npm audit fix

vulnerabilities.description: Multiple vulnerabilities in Next.js 14.2.35: HTTP request smuggling in rewrites (GHSA-ggv3-7p47-pfv8), Image Optimizer DoS (GHSA-9g9p-9gw9-jx7f), XSS in CSP nonces (GHSA-ffhc-5mcf-pf4q). Update to 15.0.0+
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Update Next.js to version 15.0.0 or later. Test thoroughly after upgrade for breaking changes

vulnerabilities.description: Insecure file permissions: Memory JSON created with mode rw-rw-r-- (664). Sensitive data stored in plaintext readable by any system user. Potential exposure of configuration or credentials.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use fs.writeFileSync(MEMORY_FILE, data, {mode: 0o600}) to restrict to owner only

vulnerabilities.description: Temporary files created without explicit permissions (rw-rw-r--). GitHub content (issues, PRs, comments) written to readable temp files. Readable by any system user.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Use fs.writeFileSync(tmpFile, body, {mode: 0o600}) or fs.mkdtemp with restricted permissions

vulnerabilities.description: Weak session ID generation: Uses Date.now() instead of cryptographic randomness. Session IDs are predictable, allowing potential session hijacking attacks.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Replace session ID generation: const sessionId = `session-${crypto.randomBytes(16).toString('hex')}`

vulnerabilities.description: PostCSS XSS vulnerability (GHSA-qx2v-qp2m-jg93) in versions <8.5.10. Unescaped </style> in CSS stringify output. Affects Next.js build process.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Verify postcss is updated to 8.5.10+ via npm update postcss

vulnerabilities.description: Session JSON files created without explicit permissions (rw-rw-r--). Session context readable by other system users. May contain sensitive developer information.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Set mode 0o600 when writing session files to restrict to owner only

vulnerabilities.description: Silent error handling: JSON parse errors caught and ignored without logging. Corrupted memory.json files fail silently, potentially losing application state without alerting user.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Log parse errors: catch (e) { console.error('Failed to parse memory:', e); }

vulnerabilities.description: GA_MEASUREMENT_ID directly embedded in inline script via template literal. While NEXT_PUBLIC_ variables are meant to be public, ensure this is the intended value. Risk if value could be user-controlled.
vulnerabilities.recommendation: Verify NEXT_PUBLIC_GA_MEASUREMENT_ID is hardcoded in .env and never from user input. Current implementation is acceptable.

securityCheckResults.hardcodedSecrets: PASS - No API keys or credentials hardcoded in source. NEXT_PUBLIC_ env vars are intended to be public.
securityCheckResults.sqlInjection: PASS - No database operations detected. All calculations done in-memory.
securityCheckResults.xssVulnerabilities: FAIL - Dependency vulnerabilities in Next.js and PostCSS introduce XSS risks. No user-controlled HTML injection in source code.
securityCheckResults.insecureDependencies: FAIL - High severity vulnerabilities in glob, Next.js. Medium severity in PostCSS.
securityCheckResults.authenticationAuthorizationIssues: PASS - No authentication system in codebase. App is public calculator (no auth needed).
securityCheckResults.filePermissions: FAIL - Helper scripts create world-readable files (mode 664) instead of restricted (600)
securityCheckResults.cryptography: FAIL - Session IDs use predictable Date.now() instead of crypto.randomBytes()
